title: Qubit Movement-Optimized Program Generation on Zoned Neutral Atom Processors
problem: Zoned neutral atom quantum architectures segregate execution spaces for 1- and 2-qubit gates, but naively scheduled programs incur excessive intra-zone atom movement, consuming most execution time in traveling rather than computation.
motivation: Quantum fidelity improves with zoned architecture, but movement overhead becomes dominant; reducing atom transport is critical for practical quantum circuit execution.
method: Mantra rewrites quantum programs using three strategies: fountain-shaped controlled-Z (CZ) chains to group gates, ZZ-interaction protocol to eliminate interleaved 1-qubit gates, and preemptive gate scheduling. Jointly optimizes gate ordering and zone assignment to minimize atom movements.
key_novelty: Fountain-shaped CZ chain topology and ZZ-interaction protocol to decouple 1- and 2-qubit gate execution streams, reducing zone transitions.
contributions: Three compilation strategies for zoned neutral atom architectures
68% reduction in inter-zone movements, 35% reduction in physical gate count
17% circuit fidelity improvement over standard execution

metrics.speedup: 68% movement reduction, 35% gate reduction, 17% fidelity gain

limitations: Specific to zoned neutral atom topology; not discussed for other quantum architectures.
primary_theme: quantum circuit optimization for zoned neutral atoms
